General UI layout, to adjust the balance between easy access to info vs text/tile size. Cogmind was originally designed for the Full layout, but as that arrangement is only suitable for players with physically large displays, other options allow one to hide info in modal windows in exchange for increased text size. Changing this requires manual restart to take effect.

HUD information is more detailed in tactical mode. Speed-related variables are shown in real time unit costs, energy and heat change predictions shown for both stationary (per turn) and mobile (per move) circumstances (latter suffers short-term inaccuracies due to averaging), items display rating as part of their respective map labels, and more. For advanced players.

Upload score sheet on death or victory for leaderboard inclusion and stat analysis (requires active internet connection). Scores for anonymous players are not uploaded, and by law you must be at least {n} years of age to activate uploads. See COGMIND-README.txt for information on the privacy policy. Leaderboards can be found here: gridsagegames.com/cogmind/scores/

{n}% chance to use a melee weapon to deflect each incoming projectile, with a second melee weapon adding {n}%, and an additional {n}% for each after that. For example, three melee weapons have a collective {n}% chance to deflect each projectile. Melee weapons successfully deflecting projectiles in this manner have a {n}% chance to take {n} damage each time.

On certain monitors, tileset users might benefit from an increase in floor brightness to better differentiate current FOV from explored areas. Each level slightly increases the brightness of floor and debris tiles. Note that while this feature is meant for use in tileset mode, increasing it also adjusts the ASCII floor color (which doesn't really need it).

Download Complex 0b10 records about the given robot variant, conferring +{n}% to hit and +{n}% damage against it, as well as {n}% to its accuracy when under fire from one. When manually hacking for analyses, a general robot class name can be entered instead of a specific variant in order to automatically choose a variant relevant at the current depth.

Automatically upload a small log file if the game crashes to help remove the problem from future releases (requires active internet connection). Upload contains no personal information--pure game log text only (see run.log). Note that the crash log does not upload until the next time Cogmind is run, to ensure a stable upload environment.

AOE damage is often spread across each target in the area of effect, dividing the damage into separate chunks before affecting a robot, where each chunk of damage selects its own target part (though they may overlap). Some explosive effects have a static number of chunks, while others randomly select from within a range for each attack.

Hides the cursor and enables keyboard-controlled map look functionality. For hardcore keyboard-only players (playing this way is FAST). Note that in Keyboard Mode, context help in the status/data windows is still available via up/down arrows. Pressing F2 while on the main interface also swaps in and out of this mode for convenience.

Stability represents the ability of this power source to generate energy while overloaded without suffering any negative side-effects. Overloading doubles output and heat. If N/A, this power source cannot be overloaded; only cooled power sources support overloading. Activate an applicable power source a second time to overload it.

Makes color-based adjustments to the interface that may help some players. Neutral 0b10 bots show as light gray instead of green, most orange UI colors instead appear azure blue, and most green is converted to light gray. Fully applying this option requires a manual restart. See the manual's Accessibility section for more info.

Download the given schematic, making it possible to build this robot at a Fabricator. Review all known schematics from the Status window. When manually hacking for schematics, a general robot class name can be entered instead of a specific variant in order to automatically choose a variant relevant at the current depth.

Automatically check for a new version of Cogmind each time the game is run (requires active internet connection). All this feature does is check www.gridsagegames.com for the newest release number and possibly some game-related news. If a newer version is available, a notice will appear in the log and on the News page.

Enables intermittent audiovisual glitch effects while system corrupted (the frequency of glitches is based on corruption level). This is intended for immersion and as a reminder of corruption, but you can turn it off if it's annoying. Disabling it also disables the window border animation when taking EM damage.

Deactivate fullscreen mode to play in a window. In windowed mode you may want to select a smaller font, or reduce the map size as desired ({n}x{n} map recommended, though with the game closed /user/system.cfg can be edited to adjust the map size). Use borderless fullscreen mode for better multimonitor support.

Ballistic weapons generally have a longer effective range and more destructive critical strikes, but suffer from less predictable damage and high recoil. Kinetic cannon hits also blast usable matter off target robots and have a chance to cause knockback depending on damage, range, and size of the target.

Meant primarily as an accessibility feature akin to closed captions, this log lists sound effects at the top-right corner of the map view, allowing anyone who keeps their volume low or muted to be able to retain access to important audio knowledge. See the manual's Audio Log section for more information.

Each flight or hover module beyond the first reduces the movement time cost by this amount, therefore increasing speed as more are attached. If not all active propulsion have the same modifier, their average value is used. Time/Move cannot normally be reduced below {n} when hovering, or {n} when flying.

Robot size category determines their likeliness of being struck by both targeted and stray shots, as well as their chance to suffer knockback. Smaller robots do not necessarily occupy their entire position, see the manual under Combat > Targeting for more about how this affects lines of fire.

Movement time penalty for being overweight, applied once if overweight at all. Penalty values for multiple different propulsion modules are averaged for calculation purposes. Further exceeding the mass support limit gradually continues to reduce speed depending on the amount of excess mass.

Alpha Access participants who joined before the deadline each have their own randomly assigned personal item. This console also doubles as an item compendium in which you can view the art for all components you've ever attached while playing, and the total number of unique items attached.

A rigged power source has been converted into a proximity mine set to detonate when anyone hostile to the creator moves adjacent to it. These power sources can no longer be attached or used for their normal purpose, but can be safely picked up and relocated by anyone not deemed a threat.

Chance for this weapon to instantly destroy the hit component, or even a robot core. (Cogmind is less susceptible to this effect, which can only destroy those parts which are already below {n}% integrity when hit.) Armor is immune to this effect, instead taking an additional {n}% damage.

Relative heat transferred to a target, where each projectile impact heats it up separately. Also the base chance to melt a part on a robot that is already overheating at the time of heat transfer. Overloaded thermal weapons transfer heat at one level higher than their normal amount.

While active, not considered a threat to Complex 0b10, but loses validity with each move. Validity expires more quickly while moving in view of 0b10 combat or security bots, and attacking any target immediately invalidates the mask. Also prevents Complex 0b10 traps from triggering.

Chance this projectile may penetrate each consecutive object it hits, e.g. {n} / {n} / {n} may pass through up to three objects, with a {n}% chance for the first, followed by {n}% and {n}% for the remaining two. Huge robots count as a single object for penetration purposes.

Amount by which the salvage potential of a given robot is affected each time shot by a projectile from this weapon. While usually negative, reducing the amount of usable salvage, some special weapons may increase salvage by disabling a robot with minimal collateral damage.

Number of milliseconds for which to block all movement commands after seeing a new enemy (or only non-disarmed threats if Stop on Threats Only is on). Enemies that move in and out of view will not trigger the block until they haven't been seen for at least {n} turns.

Amount by which the salvage potential of a given robot is affected by being engulfed in this explosion. While usually negative, reducing the amount of usable salvage, some special weapons may increase salvage by disabling a robot with minimal collateral damage.

Reinforcements dispatched by Heavies due to sensor detection of anyone using a Spoofer instead target some area on the opposite side of the Heavy from where the actual detection is made, where possible, or at closest will target the Heavy's position itself.

Determines how newly seen areas are added to the FOV. "Delay" waits until the end of an action, "Instant" updates every frame if obstacles were destroyed, and "Fade In" behaves like Instant but with a short animation for the transition from unseen to seen.

Amount by which the salvage potential of a given robot is affected each time hit by this weapon. While usually negative, reducing the amount of usable salvage, some special weapons may increase salvage by disabling a robot with minimal collateral damage.

Amount of damage potential lost per space as the explosion expands from its origin. While targeting, this falloff is represented visually by the AOE color's brightness relative to the origin (this feature can be toggled via Explosion Predictions option).

Number of milliseconds for which to highlight each space previously occupied by a robot as part of their motion trail. While active, hostile robots spotting you are indicated by exclamation points rather than glowing backgrounds to avoid color confusion.

Color item labels by their respective integrity. Labels for items currently out of view appear slightly darker. Note that even while this option is inactive, the gray scheme's colors are darkened for those items with less than {n}% integrity remaining.

Relative heat transferred to a target, where a single explosion can only affect the target once regardless of how many chunks the damage is spread over. Also the chance to melt a part on a robot that is already overheating at the time of heat transfer.

Automatically labels any robot or part under the examine mode cursor (in Keyboard Mode), or under the mouse cursor when not in Keyboard Mode (note that with the mouse cursor, holding Ctrl-Shift has the same effect even while this option is disabled).

Displays alpha supporter item attributions below the item info, and also whether you've attached that item to add it to your art gallery. Even without this option on, labels for items not previously collected are marked with a '!' following the name.

Current font set, which indirectly determines the default dimensions of the window/interface. (Note: The smallest size, {n}, does not support tilesets and is therefore only available in ASCII mode. Also in modal UI layouts, the minimum size is {n}.)

Explorer is relatively easy, Adventurer is fairly challenging, and Rogue is extremely hard (but is the mode Cogmind was designed for). See the manual for details about each mode. Changes to this setting will not take effect until starting a new run.

Thermal weapons generally have a shorter effective range, but benefit from a more easily predictable damage potential and little or no recoil. Thermal damage also generally transfers heat to the target, and may cause meltdowns in hot enough targets.

This is a direct modifier to the time it takes to fire the weapon. Some weapons are inherently faster or slower to fire. Multiple negative-delay weapons cannot contribute more than {n} to the volley firing time, but positive values have no such cap.

Total angle within which projectiles are randomly distributed around the target, spreading them along an arc of a circle centered on the shot origin. Improved targeting has no effect on the spread, which is always centered around the line of fire.

Energy drained by active propulsion units per move. The speed-adjusted per-turn value is shown in parenthesis. When slow, total movement costs are lower when averaged over multiple turns; when fast, they're higher due to multiple moves per turn.

Enables full recovery of all salvagable parts from a target, which take no further damage from the salvaging process and cannot be fried, melted, or corrupted. No effect on matter recovery, and cannot interfere with self-destruction routines.

Heat generated by active propulsion units per move. The speed-adjusted per-turn value is shown in parenthesis. When slow, total heat generation is lower when averaged over multiple turns; when fast, it's higher due to multiple moves per turn.

Enables long-distance communication with Warlord forces to determine their composition and hiding locations. Toggle active state to temporarily list all squads in the area. If active while near a squad, will signal it to emerge and assist.

Allow achievements to be earned even in challenge modes and special modes. Some are much easier in these modes compared to the regular game, even unintentionally, so a portion of players prefer to block them except when playing normally.

Actively interfere with the local combat network's offensive coordination calculations, reducing the accuracy of this bot by {n}%, and that of all 0b10 combat bots within a range of {n}. Effect stacks when installed on multiple bots.

Records the type and number of every part previously used, and provides access to information about each. Use letter keys to skip to parts beginning with that letter, and other directional/scrolling keys to navigate through the list.

Openly share the local combat network's defensive coordination values, giving yourself and all allies {n}% better accuracy against this and all 0b10 combat bots within a range of {n}. Effect stacks when installed on multiple bots.

Shows contextual tutorial messages in the log window. Each message is only shown once, but toggling this off and on again resets all message records, in addition to causing the next three runs to start in the tutorial map layout.

Shows the path to the cursor (no effect in Keyboard Mode). Note that even with this feature off, you can still hold Ctrl-Alt to highlight the path manually when necessary, and while on those keys can be used to brighten the path.

A range of minor buffs and mechanical adjustments here take the edge off the unforgiving Rogue mode. Getting far will still take experience and persistence, but it's not quite as intense. Adventurers are Rogues in training.

Entropic weapons are capable of inflicting significant, if variable, damage over long ranges, and cannot be resisted by anything but energy-based shields. However, the weapon itself is always damaged in the firing process.

Blocks vi-key input (hjklyubn), to prevent unintended movement from accidental key presses for those who don't use vi-keys anyway. Note that if this option is set, rebinding vi-keys to something else will not be possible!

Reports in real time the position and type of all robots near this terminal. The range of this effect is dependent on terminal level: {n} for Security Level {n}, {n} on level {n} terminals, and {n} on all other terminals.

Enables both real-time tracking of 0b10 Haulers across the entire floor, and gives access to their current manifest. Toggle active state to temporarily list all inventories in view. Only applies in 0b10-controlled areas.

Chance for this weapon to inflict twice as much damage and further delay both attacker and target's next opportunity to act by {n} turn. The attacker is not delayed if this effect is a property of a non-melee weapon.

Rating is a relative indicator of the item's usefulness and/or value. When comparing items, the quickest and easiest method is to go with whatever has the highest rating. However, prototypes are almost always better than common parts with a similar rating (generally implying a +{n} to their listed rating).
Faulty prototypes will almost always malfunction and have potentially serious side-effects when attached, and cannot be used or repaired, but may be scanned to obtain the schematic.
Current state of this item. This message will provide more context for special states.
General classification of this item.
Type of slot the part can be attached to, if applicable. Larger items may occupy multiple slots, both in the inventory and when attached.
Mass of an attached item contributes to a robot's total mass and affects its movement speed. Items held in inventory do not count towards total mass for movement calculation purposes.
Non-part items cannot be attached, but have other special uses. Larger items may occupy multiple inventory slots.
Propulsion modules do not indicate their mass, as the value is already factored into their movement capabilities.
Matter consumed each turn by this part while active.
Energy consumed each turn by this part while active.
Energy storage capacity of this power source. Excess energy can be stored, but requires additional utilities.
Temporarily disabled parts may be reactivated after the indicated duration.
Corrupted parts increase system corruption when attached. Repair Stations are capable of cleaning part corruption.
Malfunctioning parts cannot be reactivated until repaired, or the malfunction is automatically resolved by leaving the part attached.
Parts currently in the process of integrating cannot be activated until the process is complete.
Will be thrown upon use, and must be retrieved to use again.
Currently overloaded. For more information about overloading propulsion, see the Burnout context help below.
Currently overloaded. For more information about overloading, see the Stability context help below.
While in drop mode, this part will drop a contained trap once per turn.
While in collection mode, this part will collect items to process.
Unstable weapons implode after the indicated remaining number of shots.
Integrated parts cannot be salvaged or otherwise acquired from a robot using them.
Fragile parts are destroyed if removed after attaching them for use. While attached, these are also marked with a colon next to their letter in the parts list, as a reminder.
Field strength remaining before this trap is no longer usable. Once installed and active, strength depletion is caused by both absorbing damage and attempts to move through the field.
Battery power remaining before this item is no longer usable. Drains {n} power per turn while active.
Constructs created by the Scrap Engine may be further modified, or even expanded in size given the right conditions. Any modification also somewhat repairs the construct's integrity.
Salvage potential represents the amount of matter that could be retrieved from the robot, assuming it can be disabled without excessive collateral damage.
Exposure represents the chance that a successful attack will hit the core.
Current temperature. At the danger threshold and above, this robot is susceptible to meltdowns from additional thermal damage.
Remaining core integrity. A robot is destroyed once its core integrity reaches zero.
Permanently broken robots may not be hacked, rewired, or otherwise manually reactivated.
This drone is temporarily inoperable without an active applicable drone bay connection.
Unpowered robots may not be hacked, rewired, or otherwise manually reactivated.
Currently offline, but most disabled robots are susceptible to rewiring via moving into them with or without a Datajack.
Robots in a dormant state may be woken by distress calls, an ally's alert, or hostiles remaining in line of sight. Robots may not be hacked or rewired while dormant.
This robot's relation with you. If inactive for some reason, this message will provide more context.
Rating summarizes the robot's overall effectiveness in combat situations, thus highly-rated robots are far more dangerous.
Momentum-based modifier for melee damage. Value will fluctuate since it is always updated based on current momentum.
Percent damage modifier for ballistic weapon attacks, applied to minimum damage though may allow some weapons to exceed their maximum damage.
Density of terrain scanning, where higher-density scans are capable of analyzing terrain much more quickly. Only useful when provided with input from a terrain scanner.
Level of additional detail that can be determined about robots outside your field of vision. Only useful when provided with input from a robot scanner.
Immune to meltdown destruction and other side effects of overheating, as well as the Meltdown critical effect.
Immune to remote hacking by Programmers, and not accessible via RIF. Cannot be rewired while core disrupted.
Immune to remote hacking by Programmers. Cannot be rewired while core disrupted.
Immune to the part-severing effects of Blade Traps, Segregators, Tearclaws, Core Strippers, and Blast/Sever/Sunder critical effects.
Immune to any core-affecting effects from critical strikes, including Destroy, Blast, Smash, and Phase.
Immune to all critical strike effects, and the core exposure effect of Core Analyzers and piercing damage.
Types of additional components required to fabricate this robot, if any.
Number of turns required to complete fabrication of this robot, at each fabricator tier.

Indicates the current propulsion type, and speed as a percentage of "average" speed ({n}%). In tactical HUD mode, an additional value represents the actual time cost to move one space (thus higher values are slower).
The amount of time required to move one space when unburdened and using only this type of propulsion. Where multiple active propulsion modules have different values, the average is used.

Inactive non-airborne propulsion modify the movement time cost by this amount while airborne. However, inactive propulsion has no adverse effect on the speed of non-airborne propulsion, including core movement.

Chargeable parts automatically recharge while attached, draining your energy at their charge rate for as many turns as necessary to fully recharge, but will never reduce your energy below {n}% capacity.

Did you know Cogmind's manual contents appear both in game and as a text file "manual.txt"? You can read the manual outside the game, or even edit the file and have the changes appear in game as well. However, for convenience and because automated updating via Steam would overwrite your modified manual, in order to facilitate maintaining your notes across versions you should instead write them in the provided user/notes.txt file. (Only basic ASCII characters are accepted; foreign language characters are ignored because the engine cannot display them.)

This one isn't even that scary unless they happen to be blocking your intended path. They'll set up a bunch of turret clusters loosely centered around a Garrison and just... wait. Don't go there unless you want to introduce them to the real boss: you! They'll probably just run away if you get too close anyway. But turrets can't run.

A cave-dwelling loser who is working for someone else, and I'm not even sure they know who. Like yeah, I "work for" MAIN.C, but only like {n}% of the time. {n}% of my time is spent terrorizing Derelicts, and the other {n}% of the time I work against MAIN.C, so it balances out. CYPHRH4X0R is best H4X0R. Analyze that!

Wow, you managed to get CY-PHR interested in you? Good luck in your future hacking endeavors, as they love to mess with the results. Keep at it and try to track them down... somewhere out there in 0b10. They're wimpy and will leave you alone for good if you can find them. Big if.

Welcome to your first Zion-integrated 0b10 terminal! Unaware Operators have no clue how to secure these things, ha! Check the roster for backup, and if you need any intel that'll take longer so we'll sever this connection and you can retrieve it at the next terminal.

They won't come after you directly, and take a while to assimilate the locals, but if you let them reach critical mass you will be in serious trouble. Even worse, getting spotted by 1B-0RG himself will instantly let all Borg know exactly where you are.

They could be anywhere, or anyone. Be very wary of anything that moves. Destroying their true combat form damages their core, but you can cause the most damage once they're fully revealed, though they'll definitely run in that case, and fast.

This is a tough one, they are really good at hiding in the walls and will wait for you to get close before springing an attack. I guess you can use a Structural Scanner to help prevent being caught completely by surprise.

They will avoid you and gradually dispatch drone squads to different map locations from which to stage indirect attacks. If you find individual drones, those are probably defensive in nature and QV-33N could be nearby.

Range of electromagnetic spectrum, with narrower ranges more likely to trigger chain explosions in power sources. (AOE spectrum only affects power sources being used by Cogmind, or those exposed on the ground.)

Co-opts this terminal to aid in hacking other machines. Confers a +{n}% to hacks, while the benefit of each additional botnet terminal is halved (+{n}%, +{n}%), with each terminal providing no less than +{n}%.

Primarily for those interested in discovering more of the story and exploring various areas of the world that are otherwise much more difficult to reach in other modes. Or just running around shooting things.

BL-1NK has a problem staying in one place during fights, but that's also your problem if you're hoping to use terrain to your advantage. Setting up an ambush could be hard... maybe a Triangulator would help!

Format to which the message log is output when the game ends (has no impact on the stat summary output). Log contents are written to the scores subdirectory. This setting also applies to mid-run stat dumps.

Amount of concentrated damage required to overcome this object's armor to disable or destroy it. After resistances are factored in, the damage from a single hit must be greater than or equal to this value.

Level of detail shown in the combat log. There are numerous related features available depending on your layout and detail settings. See the manual under Advanced UI > Combat Log Window for these options.

Maximum radius of the explosion from its origin. Directional explosions only radiate outward along an arc of the specified number of degrees, centered on the projectile's approach to its point of impact.

Cogmind is technically designed and balanced for this mode, which can be reliably overcome given sufficient experience and skill, but it will put your strategic and tactical analysis skills to the test.

Guided weapons fire projectiles that follow a set path designated by a number of waypoints up to this value. Guided projectiles always hit their target. If N/A, this weapon only supports direct firing.
This Garrison Access is waiting for internal defensive forces to be replenished. Using a Signal Interpreter provides the precise number of turns remaining until the Garrison is once again on standby.
Intercepts tactical planning and coordination transmissions, providing self and all controllable allies with a +{n}% accuracy bonus against hostile Complex 0b10 combat robots within a range of {n}.
Shoot a hostile robot with a Remote Datajack to reboot or assimilate them. Can also rewire disabled targets. While Remote Datajack active, valid rewire targets blink white, hack targets blink pink.
Trick system into believing it is allied with Cogmind. After {n} turns the network will perform an automated quickboot to restore it to normal, a process which takes anywhere from {n} to {n} turns.
Chance for this weapon to automatically maximize the amount of system corruption inflicted on the target. If target is Cogmind, the amount of corruption is randomized from {n}-{n}% of the damage.
Map panning speed when cursor is at the edge of the screen, measured in milliseconds/cell (therefore high numbers are slower). Set to {n} to deactivate. Only compatible with True Fullscreen mode.
Read system data to learn more about its current state and capabilities. Also identifies all parts, and adds them to the item gallery if not already there. Parsing friendlies will not anger them.
Heat generated each turn by active parts. Here it is graphed relative to heat dissipation. Generating more heat than dissipated causes a buildup that can eventually have negative side effects.
Strength {n}: Robot scan signals accurately reflect target size and specific class rating, are unaffected by system corruption, and can discern dormant, unpowered, disabled, and broken robots.
Can also move into a Terminal's interactive part to reconfigure it, wiping all direct hacks and applying a modifier to all subsequent indirect hacks, but causing tracing to begin immediately.
This Garrison Access is communicating with additional reinforcements preparing for dispatch. Using a Signal Interpreter provides the precise number of turns remaining until the next dispatch.
Opportunistically gathers and reports on potentially useful intel remotely extracted from vulnerable Complex 0b10 networks. Must be installed on multiple terminals before it can take effect.
Energy supplied each turn by the core and all active power sources, required for moving, firing, and sustaining the operation of some utility systems. Here it is graphed relative to upkeep.
Rewrite all system data, permanently converting it into a fully controllable ally. Requires {n} turns to complete the process. Also fully penetrates systems of all bots contained within.
Dedicated interface for browsing achievements. Note that if a challenge mode is active, the only achievements that can be earned during that run are those for winning a challenge mode.
Destabilize power systems to generate a wave of energy which can be analyzed to temporarily pinpoint robots at a distance. Beyond a range of {n} the echo becomes too weak to be useful.
Use an active Recalibrator to repair a non-hostile robot via force melee movement. While Recalibrator active, repairable targets blink white. Cannot repair targets currently in combat.
Range of electromagnetic spectrum, with narrower ranges more likely to trigger chain explosions in power sources. (Cogmind's power sources are immune to this effect from projectiles.)
While powerful, explosives generally spread damage across each target in the area of effect. Explosions also tend to reduce the amount of salvage remaining after destroying a target.
Speed is represented as a percentage of "average" speed ({n}%). In tactical HUD mode, the actual time cost to move one space is shown in parenthesis (thus higher values are slower).
While active, internalizes information about any identified items seen in the open or used by robots, attempting to create new relevant schematics over time based on that knowledge.
Automatically activates parts as they are attached (when possible). This option can be toggled in realtime with Ctrl-F10 if you need to temporarily change it for a specific action.
Tap into system's combat decision-making processes in real time, increasing your accuracy and damage against this bot by {n}% while also impairing its accuracy against you by {n}%.
Offers some clarity as to X0-1V1's current mood and level of amusement. X0-1V1's amusement also falls somewhat more quickly over time if not keeping an eye on it with this active.
Induce an energy anomaly resembling a long-range distress signal that will attract nearby patrols and Sentries/Heavies to investigate. Anomaly detectable up to a range of {n}.
While active, eventually teleports to a random nearby location, removing some attached part in the process, but possibly restoring one as well if suitable slots are available.
Chance for this weapon to apply the same amount of damage to the core or a second part, ignoring coverage, and if not destroyed then the second part is knocked to the ground.
Chance for this weapon to instantly cause robot meltdown regardless of what part was hit. (Cogmind is less susceptible to this effect, instead gaining damage*{n} extra heat.)
Exposure represents the chance that a successful incoming attack will hit the core. Attach more high-coverage parts to reduce this value and protect the core from damage.
Your component with the highest coverage is not armor, which is a little worrying. I hope you have spare parts and easy access to a good mechanic. I can recommend CR-KLE.
